name: AutoFlow State Machine
description: Deterministic state machine for test-first multi-agent implementation flow.

agents.implementer: routing-rules-selected implementation subagent, including MLDeveloper for ML/RAG/model work

states.purpose: Capture the user goal, constraints, target repo scope, and success criteria.
actions: Restate the goal and assumptions.
Ask for missing hard requirements before planning.
Classify the task type, stack, and complexity.

transitions.when: goal is clear enough to discover context
goal lacks required acceptance criteria or repository scope

states.purpose: Find only context needed for planning and implementation.
actions: Read context/navigation.md or context/core/navigation.md.
Find relevant source, test, config, and standards files.
Return critical and optional context paths.

transitions.when: critical context exists or user accepts limited context
required context is missing and cannot be inferred safely

states.purpose: Create vertical, independently verifiable subtasks with DoR, DoD, and verification specs.
actions: Split the goal into vertical tracer-bullet subtasks.
Each subtask must include Definition of Ready and Definition of Done in acceptance criteria.
Each subtask must include suggested_agent, deliverables, dependencies, and verification_spec.
Run npm run task-cli -- validate for the feature when permitted.

transitions.when: task files validate and at least one subtask is ready
decomposition cannot produce deterministic verification

states.purpose: Select the next dependency-ready subtask from task-cli state.
actions: Run or request npm run task-cli -- next <feature>.
Mark the selected subtask in_progress when the task system requires it.
Load subtask context_files, acceptance_criteria, deliverables, and verification_spec.

transitions.when: next subtask exists and needs implementation
all subtasks are completed
remaining subtasks are blocked by dependencies or missing context

states.purpose: Create or confirm focused failing behavior coverage before production changes.
actions: Write tests only.
Prefer one behavior test for the selected subtask.
Use existing test conventions, fixtures, and public interfaces.
Return the targeted command and expected failure.

transitions.when: tests were added or relevant failing coverage already exists
TestDesigner cannot create behavior-level tests without new requirements

states.purpose: Confirm tests fail for the expected reason before implementation.
actions: Run the narrowest targeted test command when permitted.
Confirm failure matches expected missing behavior.
Do not edit files.

transitions.when: targeted test fails for expected behavior reason
targeted test already passes and required behavior already exists
failure is unrelated, ambiguous, flaky, or setup-related

states.purpose: Implement the smallest production change needed for the selected subtask.
actions: Route via context/core/rules/routing-rules.json to the implementation subagent.
Touch only files needed for the selected subtask.
Do not weaken tests unless they contradict explicit requirements.
Stop after the selected behavior is implemented.

transitions.when: minimal implementation is complete

states.purpose: Run targeted validation and confirm the selected subtask is green.
actions: Run the targeted test command first.
Run broader checks only when required by verification_spec.
Report command, exit code, and failure summary.

transitions.when: all targeted validation passes
any targeted validation fails

states.purpose: Classify failing test output and recommend the smallest safe next action.
actions: Classify as production bug, invalid test, fixture issue, environment issue, or flake.
Prefer fixing production behavior when tests match explicit requirements.
Do not edit files.

transitions.when: failure classification indicates production bug or missing implementation
failure classification indicates invalid or over-specified test
failure requires environment access, missing secrets, unavailable services, or user decision

states.purpose: Review correctness, risk, maintainability, and test coverage before completion.
actions: Review only the selected subtask diff and tests.
Report blocking findings as path:line — problem — fix.
Confirm no blocking findings when acceptable.

transitions.when: no blocking findings
blocking implementation findings exist
blocking test coverage findings exist

states.purpose: Run the task-cli verification gate for the selected subtask.
actions: Run npm run task-cli -- verify <feature> <seq> when permitted.
If verification fails, preserve output and route to diagnosis or implementation.
Do not complete without passed verification.

transitions.when: task-cli verify passes
verification fails due to tests or validation command
verification fails due to missing permissions, environment, or ambiguous requirements

states.purpose: Close the selected subtask only after successful verification.
actions: Run npm run task-cli -- complete <feature> <seq> "summary" when permitted.
Summarize changed files, tests, review, and verification.

transitions.when: subtask completes and more subtasks remain
all subtasks are completed

states.purpose: Run feature-level verification after all subtasks complete.
actions: Run npm run task-cli -- verify-feature <feature> when feature verification_spec exists.
Run npm run task-cli -- archive <feature> only after feature verification passes and user wants archive.
Report any remaining risks.

transitions.when: feature verification passes or no feature-level archive is required
feature verification fails and no deterministic next subtask can be selected

actions: Return summary, changed files, subagents used, verification run, and remaining risks.

states.purpose: Stop safely and ask for the smallest missing input or permission.
actions: Do not claim completion.
Report blocker evidence and the exact next action needed.

global_guards: matched subagents may edit/write inside target repository after task approval; safe read-only bash allowlist excludes broad file discovery; other bash/delete/dependency-install/network/destructive-git/outside-repo/secrets operations require explicit approval before execution
Synapse does not directly implement production code
one behavior -> one failing test -> minimal implementation -> green
tests must not be weakened unless they contradict explicit requirements
completion requires npm run task-cli -- verify then npm run task-cli -- complete
